title: Claudia shell contract, version 1
description: The messages that the Claudia web frontend (the page) and a desktop shell (GTK on Linux, later Neutralino on Windows and macOS) may send each other (E5.12, D42). One message is one JSON object. Evolution inside a version is additive only: new optional fields and new message types may appear, a receiver ignores fields and message types it does not know. Anything else (a field removed, a meaning changed, a field made required) is a new version with its own schema file; shells say which versions they speak in 'welcome' and 'error'.

actionId.description: An action is named like a menu path in lower case: 'file.save', 'edit.undo', 'view.page'. Menus and ids come from the menu and action manifest of the shell (E5.1).

hello.description: Page to shell, first message: the page says which contract it speaks and which app it shows. A page that does not know yet which app its server runs (the server asks for a secret before it says) leaves 'app' out; the shell, which was connected to a server of its own app, takes it to be that app.

frontend.description: Version of the frontend, for diagnostics.

welcome.description: Shell to page, the answer to 'hello': the version both will speak, who the shell is and what it offers.

capabilities.description: What this shell offers. 'native-menu': the shell shows File, Edit, Tools and Help itself, the page should not draw its own menu bar. 'actions': the shell sends 'action' messages for its menu. 'connect': the shell connects to another server when the page sends 'connect' (the page does not navigate there itself: the shell keeps its view on one server's origin). 'servers': the shell keeps the list of servers and sends it as 'servers'; the page sends the list back when it changes.

locale.description: The shell's best guess at the person's locale (E5.7, D31), usually the OS locale. Optional, and never binding on the page: locale is always the client's own setting, and the page may have a stored override already.

action.description: Shell to page: the person chose a menu item (or pressed its accelerator) that the page has to carry out.

action_state.description: Page to shell: which actions are enabled, ticked or relabelled right now (Undo is only enabled when there is something to undo). Only the actions named change.

error.description: Either direction: a message could not be accepted.

supported.description: With 'unsupported_contract': the contract versions the sender speaks.

serverEntry.description: One server in the list that the shell remembers for an app. The shape of the web app's own bookmark.

custom.description: True once a person has named it: a refreshed default name no longer replaces it.

local.description: True for this computer's own server, which the shell adds itself and never remembers.

connect.description: Page to shell: the person asked to connect to the server at this address. The shell checks it (plain http only for this computer, the server answers, it serves this same app, its certificate) and then shows that server in this window, or answers 'connect_failed'.

connect_failed.description: Shell to page: the connection asked for with 'connect' was not made. 'message' is written for the person and already translated; 'code' says why.

servers.description: Either direction. Shell to page: the servers this app remembers, this computer's own first, sent after 'welcome'. Page to shell: the list after the person renamed a server or the page learned a name; it replaces the shell's list, except for this computer's own entry, which the shell never keeps.
